message:
release: 0.2.134 -- a new hash, because the old one is what Defender objects to

Version only. No logic changes, and nothing else differs from 0.2.133.

On one company machine Windows Defender flags 0.2.133's GNLinkSetup.exe (ThreatID 2147731250) and
the in-app update dies at the staging check with "could not hash staged GNLinkSetup.exe". The
detection began on a manually downloaded copy and followed the same bytes into staging. Defender
exclusions do not hold there -- Tamper Protection and company policy own that setting -- so the
only lever left on our side is the file itself: an unsigned rebuild has a different hash, and the
cloud verdict attached to the old one does not follow it.

That is the whole reason for this release, and it is worth being plain about what it is: a
workaround aimed at one detection, not a fix for anything. A false positive on an unsigned
installer can land again on the next build just as easily.

Windows only. Android stays at 0.2.20 and build.gradle.kts is untouched.

Product: product_version.hpp. Tests: none. Docs: none.
